t:
(a) Notwithstanding section 1101, available balances of expired Architect of the Capitol appropriations shall be available to the Architect of the Capitol to make the deposit to the credit of the Employees’ Compensation Fund required by section 8147(b) of title 5, United States Code. 
    (b) Effective Date.—This section shall apply with respect to appropriations for fiscal year 2013 and each year thereafter.

fable.w: This provision only makes expired appropriation balances available to the Architect of the Capitol for a required deposit to the Employees' Compensation Fund. Every actor involved is inside the federal government, and no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any decision. There is no real tempting contrary reading; it is purely an internal appropriations and funding provision.
fable.s: available balances of expired Architect of the Capitol appropriations shall be available to the Architect of the Capitol to make the deposit to the credit of the Employees’ Compensation Fund

opus.w: This section only lets the Architect of the Capitol use leftover expired funds to make a required deposit into a federal fund. No one outside the federal government is consulted or involved. It looks like Example 1, which is also a funding provision labelled "No." Mentioning a fund or a legal requirement is a money mechanism, not a decision process that includes outside parties.
opus.s: available balances of expired Architect of the Capitol appropriations shall be available to the Architect of the Capitol to make the deposit to the credit of the Employees’ Compensation Fund required by section 8147(b) of title 5, United States Code.

qwen_chat.w: This section deals exclusively with the availability of federal appropriations for a federal fund. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are the Architect of the Capitol and the Employees’ Compensation Fund, both of which are within the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: available balances of expired Architect of the Capitol appropriations shall be available to the Architect of the Capitol to make the deposit to the credit of the Employees’ Compensation Fund
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Architect of the Capitol is a unique officer, their actions might involve external parties. However, the text strictly concerns the internal accounting and availability of federal funds for a specific federal trust fund (Employees’ Compensation Fund). There is no mention of consulting with states, the public, or any non-federal entity. The actors are the Architect of the Capitol (federal) and the Fund (federal).
